While 'N-acetylation' is listed as a variable modification, it is used as a standard search parameter for protein N-termini rather than a targeted acetylome enrichment workflow. Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The PRIDE submission PXD008693 specifically contains the HEK293 cell proteomics data. While the project description mentions human brain tissue, the metadata explicitly states that brain proteomics files are in PXD005445. The analyzed material for this submission was unfractionated lysate from HEK293-L10a cells.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: This study is a method-development/characterization project focused on isoform-level protein quantification using integrated omics (mRNA-seq, ribosome profiling, and proteomics) in HEK293 cells and human brain tissue. There is no biological perturbation, treatment, or differential case-control comparison axis defined for the proteomics data provided in this submission.

workflow: In this study, we make used of mRNA-seq... integrating this data with ribosome profiling and LC-MS/MS, to assign ribosome footprints and peptides at the isoform level.
Spectra obtained from the Orbitrap Elite... were processed using MaxQuant44 (v1.5.2.1).
The code for the modified expectation-maximization algorithm is freely available and can be found at the Github repo: https://github.com/rkitchen/EMpire
search_parameters: This search included a fixed modification, cysteine carbamidomethylation, and two variable modifications, N-acetylation and methionine oxidation.
Peptides were searched using “trypsin/P” as the digestion enzyme, with a tolerance for up to 2 missed cleavages.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The dataset is specifically designed for isoform-level proteomics rather than standard protein-level quantification. Reanalysis requires the EMpire pipeline to integrate RNA-seq priors for peptide-to-isoform allocation.
